questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my German and experience a new city. Already had a lot of love for and interest in Berlin, therefore I chose HU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Ok easy, the uni has 1 long file with all the courses in it (this file however is difficult to locate)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The int. team have an introduction class for int. students which was helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult! Lived in the dorm of the Danish church for the last 3 months but had to find urgent solutions for the months before due to a water leakage in the dorm building. Had an almost bad case of not getting my deposit back at one of the places I lived in the beginning so an important thing is: always take pictures of basically everything when you move in!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: to my knowledge the on-campus opportunities are pretty far out in the city (sometimes outside the Ring)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The international team at HU were very nice and helpful. German unis are however very analogue and the website a bit complicated (especially when you're in the beginning of your German improvement curve!)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The int. team have an introduction class for int. students where they give the information. roam around the HU website before to find a course list and  consider which subjects you want to participate in before getting there. registration happens 2 weeks after classes have startet (2 weeks of trying out classes therefore)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Great help from the int. team

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful! remeber to ask the professors for exam dates, that does not go through the administration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't stress it and talk with the other int. students

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not too difficult academically. My primary goal was to take as many classes in German, which I did (all of them), so that was my main challenge during the semester. Exams are oral but the professors are very nice and I would all in all recommend taking as many classes in German as you can! Also because you only get 3 points for English subjects (at least in the summer semester of 2026).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: more "tavleundervisning", good powerpoints, almost no preparatory readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Zugang zum Recht & Unmet Legal Needs – 5 ECTS
Verhandlung, Abschluss und gerichtliche Durchsetzung grenzüberschreitender Verträge – 5 ECTS
Ökonomische Analyse des Rechts – 5 ECTS
Deutsch als Fremdsprach B2.2 – 5 ECTS
Sicherheitspolitische Perspektiven des Europarechts – 5 ECTS
Europäisches Strafrecht – 5 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above! Sicherheitspolitische Perspektiven des Europarechts was the most difficult, Mr. Ruffert is very good and demanding.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Friends told me HU Sport was great! Didn't try it myself though.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Freiluftskino, the wonderful Stadtbäder of Berlin, using your free public transportation to go to Grunewald, Potsdam and Leipzig and much more! Berlin has many free or low-cost fun opportunities for students I would say

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: explore the city and its many Bezirken - get a bike fast!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Speak German (also when you make mistakes!), go out into the city, don't stay home too much, make sure you translate the lessons throughout the semester and not in the end, as you'll then actually have an ok stressed exam season. Take classes from Hr. Klöhn and Hr. Ruffert!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends <3 new home city <3 German skills!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: German grammar, school adm. stuff, missing CPH (but that was always only a flixbus-trip away!)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
